DataSource.description:
How a point gets its value, and so how the poll scheduler treats it.

============  =================================================================================================
SHORT_POLL    Polled at its polling interval in the device's regular cyclic schedule (the default).
LONG_POLL     Polled at its polling interval, but in a separate schedule so that very long intervals (totals,
              configuration registers) do not stretch the hyperperiod of the regular schedule.
POLL_ONCE     Read once when the device is set up or reconfigured (nameplate data), then never polled.
STATIC        Never read from a device: the value is configuration or whatever was last written to it.
NEVER_POLL    A device point the platform never polls; values arrive by push (change of value, unsolicited
              responses) or by an explicit get. ``never`` is accepted as an older spelling.
SERVER        A served point of a device in a server role: written by the platform and by the peer's pushes,
              never polled, seeded both ways when the device registers with its proxy.
============  =================================================================================================

Points that are not ``scheduled`` are left out of the cyclic poll sets; points that are not ``polled`` are never
read by the scheduler at all, so their staleness is judged by any configured ``stale_timeout`` alone.
DataSource.title: DataSource

point.description:
One registry row: a 2030.5 attribute of the device's resources, in the interoperability convention.

Column headers as the discovery tooling writes them (and the legacy agent's ``Parameter Type``) are accepted
alongside snake_case. In the client role rows under the upward resources are writable by default and rows under the
controls are not; a served row (``data_source: server``) is the mirror image: the platform writes the controls and
the DER client reports the upward resources (``remote_writable``).

Addressing.description:
How addresses in the registry are expressed.

offset: the zero-based protocol address (default; 'exact' is accepted as a synonym).
offset_plus: one-based, as printed in many vendor manuals; 1 is subtracted.
address: table-prefixed one-based (1, 10001, 30001, 40001 ranges); the table base is subtracted.

MessageBusConfig.description:
Configuration for a single remote message bus connection.

Every field other than ``name`` is forwarded to the protocol proxy process as a
command line argument (``--field-name value``), so field names must match the
proxy class's constructor parameters. ``extra='allow'`` lets bus types without a
dedicated config class pass arbitrary parameters through to their proxy.

mode.description: How the adapter bridges VOLTTRON and the remote bus. "translate": local device publications are transformed into the remote topic's format here, and a remote message for a device is written through the Resource Bridge's write RPC (see resource_bridge) or, for a remote-owned resource, published locally in the canonical format. "relay": OpenFMB (or any aliased format) lives on the VOLTTRON bus itself under the remote topic; the adapter only re-serialises between the remote encoding and the local JSON form, and the Resource Bridge does the translating.

BridgeConfig.description:
One direction of mirroring: every message of ``source`` is transformed into the format of ``target`` (the chain
the presentation service chooses for the fields the message carries) and written to it, or published on it.

name.description: Stable handle for the bridge; defaults to "<source>><target>".
name.title: Name

points.description: Only these source points are bridged (device sources; all by default).
points.title: Points

source.description: Where messages come from: a device (its publications) or a bus topic.

target.description: Where they go: a device (written through the driver) or a bus topic (published).

write_unchanged.description: Write a point again even when its value is the one last written to the target (by default only changes are written).
write_unchanged.title: Write Unchanged

BridgeConfig.title: BridgeConfig

EndConfig.description:
One end of a bridge: a UAI the presentation service knows. A *device* end (the default) is the canonical device
the UAI leads to, read from its publications or written through the driver. A *bus* end is the UAI itself as a
topic on the VOLTTRON bus carrying messages in the UAI's (alias) format: an OpenFMB profile topic, read from or
published to, so OpenFMB-aware agents and the Message Bus Adapter in relay mode can take part.

bus.description: Treat the UAI as a topic on the VOLTTRON bus rather than as a device.
bus.title: Bus

topic.description: Bus end only: the topic, when it is not the UAI joined with "/".
topic.title: Topic

EndConfig.title: EndConfig

chain_cache_size.description: Chains kept per bridge, one per distinct set of fields a publication carried.
chain_cache_size.title: Chain Cache Size

driver.description: VIP identity of the platform driver that owns the targets.
driver.title: Driver

echo_window.description: Seconds during which a publication that merely confirms a value this agent wrote to that device is not bridged back.
echo_window.title: Echo Window

presentation_service.description: VIP identity of the interoperability (presentation) service.
presentation_service.title: Presentation Service

result_topic_prefix.description: Each bridge publishes the outcome of every write on <prefix>/<bridge key>.
result_topic_prefix.title: Result Topic Prefix

stale_after.description: Before deciding whether a target point needs writing, ask the driver (its last RPC) for points whose last known value is older than this many seconds or unknown. Unset: rely on the target's publications and this agent's own writes only.
stale_after.title: Stale After
